about: Wrong answers that point to a specific misunderstanding about measurement and geometry. 'pointsTo' is the subskill to work on. Claude's draft (2026-11-21), waiting for owner review.

misconceptions.description: Divides when converting to a smaller unit (or multiplies going to a bigger one): 5 feet = 5/12 inch.
Uses the wrong conversion number, often 10 or 100 for customary units: 1 foot = 10 inches.
Stops after one step of a two-step conversion: 2 yards = 6 (feet, not inches).
Adds the two conversion numbers instead of multiplying: 1 yard = 3 + 12 inches.
Mixes up area (squares inside) and perimeter (distance around).
Adds only the two labelled sides for a rectangle's perimeter (it has four).
Adds only the labelled sides of an L-shape, leaving out the sides that weren't labelled.
Uses the slanted side instead of the height for a parallelogram's area.
Subtracts instead of dividing to find a missing side from the area.
Forgets the ½ in a triangle's (or trapezoid's) area: base × height.
Uses only one base for a trapezoid's area (it's the average of the two bases × height).
Finds the area of the whole rectangle around an L-shape, without taking the cut corner away.
Splits an L-shape into pieces that overlap, counting a corner twice.
Uses the diameter where the formula needs the radius (or the other way round).
Mixes up the circle formulas: πr² for the circumference, or 2πr for the area.
Forgets to halve for a half circle.
Adds the measurements (or forgets to square the radius) instead of multiplying: volume = l + w + h.
Finds the surface area (the faces) instead of the volume (the space inside).
Forgets the ⅓ in a cone's volume.
